§01 · WHY CLUSTERS03 / 23
The probe

Cluster abundance
is a growth-of-structure
probe of dark energy.

The number density of clusters as a function of mass and redshift, dN/dM dz, is exponentially sensitive to σ₈ and the dark-energy equation of state — complementary to lensing and clustering. LSST will deliver ≳10⁵ clusters.

Weinberg+ 2013 · DES 2020
Cumulative cluster counts · z = 0.4 ± 0.05 · sensitivity to w  ·  Weinberg et al. 2013

§02 · THE PROBLEM05 / 23
How optical finders work

Find the red sequence,
count the members,
call it richness λ.

redMaPPer & friends identify overdensities of red, passively-evolving galaxies at a common redshift. Richness λ is the mass proxy — cheap, photometric, and available over the whole survey.

Rykoff+ 2014 · redMaPPer
Composite red sequence · 0.25 < z < 0.26  ·  Rykoff et al. 2014 (redMaPPer)
§02 · PROJECTION06 / 23
P(λ_obs | λ_true, z) · correlated LSS boosts the projection tail  ·  Costanzi et al. 2019
Systematic #1

Projection effects.

The red sequence is a 2D selection. Uncorrelated and correlated structure along the line of sight gets counted into λ, inflating richness at fixed halo mass — and, worse, doing so anisotropically and in a mass-dependent way.

Lucey 1983 · Rozo+ 2015 · Costanzi+ 2019 · Sunayama+ 2020 · Wu+ 2022
§02 · CAUGHT IN THE ACT
Spectroscopic proof · DESI

Projection is real — and worse
exactly where it hurts.

Mean projected-member fraction f_proj & richness bias vs richness · z∼0.1 and z∼0.2  ·  Myles et al. 2025 (DESI)

DESI line-of-sight velocities show f_proj is more than 2× larger at low richness, plus the first spectroscopic evidence that projection grows with redshift — by ~25% from z∼0.1 to z∼0.2.

§02 · THE FALLOUT
Why projection is so corrosive

Three consequences.

01
Inflated, skewed richness–mass scatter

Projection adds a non-Gaussian tail to P(λ|M): low-mass halos scatter up into rich bins.

02
Mis-centering

The chosen central is not always the true BCG / halo center, biasing stacked lensing profiles.

03
Selection bias in the lensing signal

Preferentially selecting line-of-sight-aligned systems correlates λ with orientation → biased ⟨M|λ⟩.

Sohn+ 2018 · Myles+ 2021 · Wu+ 2022 · Salcedo+ 2025
§02 · THE COSMOLOGY COST08 / 23
The bottom line for cosmology

Miscalibrate the selection,
bias the cosmology.

Optical cluster cosmology has historically pulled low σ₈/S₈ when projection and selection effects are under-modeled. Enormous effort now goes into forward-modeling these effects — but it may be worth selecting clusters a different way.

Costanzi+ 2019 · Sunayama+ 2024 · Zhou 2024 · Myles+ 2025 · Yang+ 2026
Ω_m–S₈ · SDSS redMaPPer clusters vs eFEDS / DES / SPT-SZ  ·  Sunayama et al. 2024
§03 · A DIFFERENT HANDLE09 / 23
The idea

The most massive
galaxies live in
clusters — and wear
their history as an
extended stellar halo.

Mergers and accretion build a diffuse envelope + intracluster light around the central. Its outskirts trace the halo, not the survey's line of sight.

Intracluster light around the BCG of Abell 85 (deep g-band)  ·  Montes 2022
§03 · DEFINITION10 / 23
Outer stellar mass, Mout
The stellar mass in a 50–100 kpc annulus around the central galaxy — a proxy that uses only the central.
~0.2 dex
SHMR scatter — rivals redMaPPer
projection-free
no line-of-sight member counting
→ lower mass
reaches groups, not just rich clusters
Huang+ 2021 · Xhakaj+ 2023 · Kwiecien+ 2025 · Zhou 2025 · Xu 2025 · Leidig 2025
§03 · THE NEW CATCH11 / 23
The trade we make
Trade projection effects for satellite contamination: a massive cluster can host more than one galaxy with high Mout.

At the very highest masses this is rare. But central-of-a-group and satellite-of-a-cluster stellar masses overlap — so contamination grows as we push Mout lower. This paper: quantify it, and knock it down with percolation.

Xhakaj+ 2023 · Kwiecien+ 2025 · Zu & Mandelbaum 2015

§04 · BUILDING Mout13 / 23
The measurement

Isophotal fits →
elliptical 50–100 kpc
annulus.

Project FoF stellar particles into 300×300 kpc maps; fit elliptical isophotes (Jedrzejewski 1987 via photutils); integrate stellar mass in the 50–100 kpc semi-major-axis annulus. 2D annulus = optimal low-scatter selection; 2D and 3D give near-identical lensing.

hydrotools · photutils · Zhou 2025 · Xu 2025
Fig. 1 — outer stellar mass measurement
§04 · PERCOLATION14 / 23
The algorithm

Sort by Mout, then
clear the neighborhood.

Thresholdcut M_out > M_min
→
Sortdescending M_out
→
Targettake the top galaxy
→
Removedrop all others within R_perc
→
Iteratedown the list

Rperc tied to the target halo's R200c, scanned from 0.75 to 3.0 R200c. Applied in projection through the full box — no line-of-sight selection (a deliberately pessimistic choice — return to this).

§05 · COMPLETENESS vs PURITY16 / 23
Result #2 · massive halo selection

Duplication vs
completeness:
a tunable trade.

Ratio of selected galaxies to true centrals per M200c bin. >1 ⇒ a halo double-counted via a surviving satellite. Small Rperc + low cut ⇒ duplication of the richest halos; larger Rperc or higher cut removes it. An Mout>10¹¹ cut: no duplication at any radius — but only the most massive halos.

Fig. 3 — selection ratio vs M₂₀₀c
§05 · WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT GOES17 / 23
Central completeness
Fig. 4 — central recovery vs M₂₀₀c  ·  ≳80% for the most massive halos
Composition of the removed
Fig. 5 — removed-central fraction vs R_perc

Removed centrals are mostly group-scale or chance line-of-sight alignments — only 13 / 175 cluster-scale centrals are removed, so cluster-scale completeness stays high.

§05 · THE SWEET SPOT18 / 23
Headline result
At Mout ≈ 4×10¹⁰ M⊙ and Rperc ≈ 2.0 R200c, outer stellar mass + simple percolation yields a cluster sample that is both highly complete and pure for halos ≳ 10¹⁴ M⊙.

And purity/completeness vary slowly near 2.0 R200c — so the method tolerates an imperfectly known percolation radius in real data.

§06 · A CAVEAT19 / 23
Honesty about the simulation

FoF over-linking inflates
the contamination.

Friends-of-friends links well-separated systems into one "halo." Satellites reach 5–6.5 R200c: ≈40% of satellites lie beyond R200c, ≈18% beyond 2, ≈5% beyond 3 — so our satellite fractions are likely over-estimates.

Fig. 6 — three cluster-scale halos: many FoF members lie well beyond R₂₀₀c (black circle)
§07 · TOWARD REAL DATA20 / 23
From TNG to the survey

What it takes to run
this on the sky.

01
An observational percolation radius

Estimate R200c from the (low-scatter) Mout proxy itself; the slow variation near 2 R200c makes this robust.

02
Redshift-space percolation

Use redshifts to reject the distant chance alignments — bounded by peculiar velocities & photo-z. Left to future work.

03
Multi-wavelength validation

Cross-check purity/completeness against X-ray and Sunyaev–Zel'dovich catalogs.

§07 · SUMMARY21 / 23
Take three things away

Summary.

→
Outer stellar mass sidesteps projection

A low-scatter (~0.2 dex), central-only cluster proxy that avoids the dominant systematic of red-sequence finders.

→
Satellite contamination is modest, and percolation helps

≤15% raw, driven well below with a simple proximity filter; better than total-stellar-mass selection at low mass.

→
A clean, calibratable selection for M ≳ 10¹⁴ M⊙

Mout≈4×10¹⁰, Rperc≈2 R200c — a promising, projection-free handle for LSST cluster cosmology.

BACKUP23 / 23
Backup / anticipated questions

Spare slides.

Why not total stellar mass?

Matched in number density, total-M contamination is similar without percolation but worse at low mass after it — Mout tracks halo, not recent central SF.

Resolution / TNG caveats

Stellar mass normalization is resolution-dependent; results depend on relative Mout ordering, not absolute scale.

Miscentering by a satellite

7 of 13 removed cluster centrals are replaced by a higher-Mout satellite of the same halo — halo kept, but miscentered.
